In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AQP4 immunostaining in active demyelination should be done in all cases, but the absence or presence of staining should not be used as the sole criteria to make a diagnosis of NMO.
AQP4 immunopathology in surgical biopsy specimens is highly specific for NMO/NMOD, with the exception of a small subset of cases with MS.

AQP4 immunostaining is not a reliable marker for the diagnosis of NMO/NOSD, but should be performed in cases of active demyelinative lesions in which AQP4 immunopathology may provide important diagnostic information.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

AQP4-II immunohistochemical staining should be performed on all biopsy specimens of active inflammatory demyelinating spinal cord lesions, and that AQP4-II immunostaining should be performed on active inflammatory demyelinative lesions in the brain if there is a high index of clinical suspicion of NMOSD.
AQP4-IgnG testing should be performed on active demyelination with astrocyte injury and granulocytes.

in the setting of active demyeling lesions, AQP4 immunostaining is helpful for distinguishing NMO from MS and should be considered in cases with atypical features, such as tumefaction, granulocytosis, and astrocyte injury, and when there is clinical suspicion of NMO.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AQP4 loss is highly suggestive of NMO and AQP4 increased is highly suggestive of MS.
